official_measurement_examples.name: HSE consultation zones
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE is a statutory consultee for relevant development around major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines and sets consultation distances within which planning authorities obtain HSE advice.

official_measurement_examples.name: Three-zone methodology
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE's Planning Advice Web App uses inner middle and outer zones plus development type, size and intensity to provide advice; proximity alone is not the full advice result.

official_measurement_examples.name: Pipeline-specific risk
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE pipeline land-use planning zones are based on quantified risk assessment using pipeline-specific attributes such as diameter, wall thickness, operating pressure, steel and burial depth.

official_measurement_examples.name: PSR scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Pipelines Safety Regulations impose general pipeline safety duties and additional duties for major accident hazard pipelines; those safety duties are not planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current HSE update
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE's MAH pipeline pages note a change in duties from 6 April 2026 for carbon capture utilisation and storage and offshore hydrogen production, so regulatory date context must be retained.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning advice not final decision
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE may advise against or not advise against planning permission, while the planning authority remains responsible for the planning decision and call-in can apply in exceptional cases.

official_measurement_examples.name: Notification lifecycle
official_measurement_examples.fact: MAH pipeline notifications occur at construction, before use and for later changes such as operator changes or major modifications; a historic notification is not proof of unchanged current status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Pipeline safety consultation, planning permission, easements, land ownership and physical connection capacity are separate questions.

core_rules: an HSE consultation zone is not automatic planning refusal
distance to a pipeline is not sufficient to reproduce HSE land-use planning advice
inner middle and outer zones must retain pipeline-specific risk context
HSE advice is not the planning authority's final decision
Pipelines Safety Regulations compliance is not planning permission
pipeline notification is not a development right
historic pipeline notification must retain lifecycle and operator-change context
a major accident hazard pipeline may have site-specific consultation distances
generic buffer distances must not replace HSE's current consultation-zone data
pipeline safety status does not determine land ownership or easement rights
gas network proximity does not prove a connection point or available capacity
EN-4 strategic policy is not a parcel-specific consent
2026 regulatory duty changes must not be backdated to earlier evidence
pipeline planning evidence does not reserve development capacity
no parcel pipeline clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official HSE and GOV.UK sources checked on 2026-07-26. Current HSE consultation-zone methodology, PSR duties and the April 2026 duty change were kept distinct from planning permission, easements and network capacity.
